judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Hero mosaic photo (model in a black sequinned top) inside the 'Get the party started / Just-arrived womenswear' link, alt "MOSAIC TILE 1858X1858 1". The alt is the CMS file name, not a description: it is exposed (the browser's link name starts with it) and a screen reader reads it inside the link. The link's visible text already gives its purpose, so the image should have alt="" or a real description; a file-name alternative is failure F30. The claim says the alternative describes something the image does not show, which in good faith points at that defect. I found no technique that makes it pass. The live page's server HTML, fetched on the day of the capture, has the same markup for this element, so the capture does not differ in a way that matters here.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: The claim says the alt describes something the image does not show, but the image does show a top, so the sentence is false as worded. The image is in a product tile link whose only text is the heading 'Shop now'; the link goes to one specific product, and the picture carries baked-in text naming it ('005 // Animal-print cape-detail top'). The live page's server HTML, fetched on the day of the capture, has the same markup for this element, so the capture does not differ in a way that matters here.
